zajjaj:36-36.t: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَ سُلَيْمانَ﴾: its meaning is "when her messenger came to Solomon (فَلَمّا جاءَ رَسُولُها سُلَيْمانَ)". It may also be "when her gift came to Solomon (فَلَمّا جاءَ بِرُّها سُلَيْمانَ)", except that His saying ﴿ارْجِعْ إلَيْهِمْ فَلَنَأْتِيَنَّهم بِجُنُودٍ لا قِبَلَ لَهم بِها ولَنُخْرِجَنَّهم مِنها أذِلَّةً وهم صاغِرُونَ﴾ [al-Naml: 37] is an address to the messenger. And His saying, the Exalted, ﴿لا قِبَلَ لَهم بِها﴾ [al-Naml: 37] means: they are not able to withstand her armies. [Translator's note: the source says "her armies" (جُنُودِها), although the pronoun in بِها refers to Solomon's armies.]

zajjaj:38-38.t: And His saying: ﴿قالَ يا أيُّها المَلأُ أيُّكم يَأْتِينِي بِعَرْشِها﴾, i.e. "her throne (سَرِيرِها)". ﴿قَبْلَ أنْ يَأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ﴾: Solomon ﷺ wished to take the throne in a way in which taking it was permissible, because had they come as Muslims, it would not have been permissible to take what was in their hands. It is also possible that Solomon wanted to display a miraculous sign by bringing the throne to himself in that very hour, since that is one of the miraculous signs.

zajjaj:39-39.t: ﴿قالَ عِفْرِيتٌ مِنَ الجِنِّ﴾: "al-ʿifrīt (العِفْرِيتُ)" is one who carries a matter through and goes to extremes in it, with malice and cunning. One says: "a man who is ʿifr, ʿifrīt, ʿifriya, nifriya and nufāriyya (رَجُلٌ عِفْرٌ، وعِفْرِيتٌ، وعِفْرِيَةٌ، نِفْرِيَةٌ، ونُفارِيَّةٌ)", all with one meaning. ﴿أنا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أنْ تَقُومَ مِن مَقامِكَ﴾, i.e. the length of your sitting that you sit with your companions; and it was said: before you rise from your seat of judgement.

zajjaj:40-40.t: And His saying: ﴿قالَ الَّذِي عِنْدَهُ عِلْمٌ مِنَ الكِتابِ﴾ — it is said that he was Āṣaf ibn Barḥiyā. ﴿أنا آتِيكَ بِهِ قَبْلَ أنْ يَرْتَدَّ إلَيْكَ طَرْفُكَ﴾, i.e. in the time it takes someone reaching out to reach the furthest point of your gaze and then return to you. It was also said: in the time it takes you to open your eye and then blink; and this is closer to "the returning of the glance (ارْتِدادِ الطَّرْفِ)". Similar to it in speech is: "he did that in the glance of an eye (فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ في لَحْظَةِ عَيْنٍ)", i.e. in the time of looking a single look. It is said in the exegesis that he called upon the Greatest Name of Allah, by which, when He is called, He answers. It was said that it is: "O Possessor of Majesty and Honour (يا ذا الجَلالِ والإكْرامِ)"; and it was said that it is: "O our God, and God of all creation, one God, there is no god but You (يا إلَهَنا، وإلَهَ الخَلْقِ جَمِيعًا، إلَهًا واحِدًا، لا إلَهَ إلّا أنْتَ)". He mentioned this name, then said: "Bring her throne (اِئْتِ بِعَرْشِها)", and when he had completed that, the throne appeared before Solomon.

zajjaj:41-41.t: And His saying: ﴿قالَ نَكِّرُوا لَها عَرْشَها نَنْظُرْ أتَهْتَدِي﴾: the jussive (jazm) in "نَنْظُرْ" is the proper form, and the reading follows it. "نَنْظُرُ" with the nominative (rafʿ) is also permissible. Whoever puts it in the jussive does so as the answer to the command (jawāb al-amr); whoever puts it in the nominative does so with the meaning "so we shall see (فَسَنَنْظُرُ)". And His saying "أتَهْتَدِي" means: will she be guided to recognising it or not.

zajjaj:42-42.t: And His saying: ﴿قالَتْ كَأنَّهُ هُوَ﴾: she did not say "it is her throne (إنَّهُ عَرْشُها)" [Translator's note: so in the source; i.e. "it is my throne"], nor did she say "it is not her throne (لَيْسَ هو بِعَرْشِها)"; she likened it to it, because it had been disguised. It is narrated that its bottom was made its top.

zajjaj:43-43.t: And His saying: ﴿وَصَدَّها ما كانَتْ تَعْبُدُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ إنَّها كانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍ كافِرِينَ﴾, i.e. the habit she was on kept her from faith, because she grew up knowing only a people who worshipped the sun, so habit kept her back. He made her habit clear by His saying: ﴿إنَّها كانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍ كافِرِينَ﴾. "أنَّها كانَتْ مِن قَوْمٍ كافِرِينَ" (with fatḥa) is also permissible, and then the meaning is: "her being from a disbelieving people kept her back (صَدَّها كَوْنُها مِن قَوْمٍ كافِرِينَ)", and it would be an explanation of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ما كانَتْ تَعْبُدُ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
And His saying: ﴿قِيلَ لَها ادْخُلِي الصَّرْحَ﴾: "al-ṣarḥ (الصَّرْحُ)" in the language is the palace, and the courtyard (al-ṣaḥn). One says: "this is the sāḥa of the house (ساحَةُ الدّارِ)", "the ṣaḥna of the house (صَحْنَةُ الدّارِ)", "the bāḥa of the house (باحَةُ الدّارِ)", "the qāʿa of the house (قاعَةُ الدّارِ)" and "the qāriʿa of the house (قارِعَةُ الدّارِ)"; all of this has the meaning of "al-ṣaḥn (الصَّحْنُ)", the courtyard.
And His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأتْهُ حَسِبَتْهُ لُجَّةً﴾, i.e. she thought it was water. A courtyard of glass had been made for Solomon, with water and fish beneath it, so she thought it was water and uncovered her shins. That was because the jinn had disparaged her shins and feet before him, and mentioned that her feet were like the hoof of a donkey; so the matter of her feet became clear.

zajjaj:45-45.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَإذا هم فَرِيقانِ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾, i.e. then Ṣāliḥ's people were two parties, a believing one and a disbelieving one, disputing, each party saying: "The truth is with me." The disbelieving party demanded the punishment as a condition for believing Ṣāliḥ, so he said: ﴿لَوْلا تَسْتَغْفِرُونَ اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكم تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ [al-Naml: 46], i.e. why did you say: "If what you have brought is true, then bring us the punishment"? ﴿لَوْلا تَسْتَغْفِرُونَ اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكم تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ [al-Naml: 46], i.e. "why do you not ask Allah's forgiveness (هَلّا تَسْتَغْفِرُونَ اللَّهَ)?"

zajjaj:47-47.t: His saying: ﴿قالُوا اطَّيَّرْنا بِكَ وبِمَن مَعَكَ﴾: the original form is "تَطَيَّرْنا"; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṭāʾ, and the alif was brought in because of the sukūn of the ṭāʾ. So when you begin with it you say: "اِطَّيَّرْنا بِكَ", and when you join it you do not pronounce the alif; it drops because it is a connective alif (alif al-waṣl). ﴿قالَ طائِرُكم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. whatever good or evil befalls you is from Allah. ﴿بَلْ أنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ تُفْتَنُونَ﴾, i.e. you are being tested. "تُفْتَنُونَ" may also be from "al-fitna (الفِتْنَةُ)", i.e. your taking of ill omens is a fitna (trial).

zajjaj:48-48.t: ﴿وَكانَ في المَدِينَةِ تِسْعَةُ رَهْطٍ يُفْسِدُونَ في الأرْضِ ولا يُصْلِحُونَ﴾: these were the most insolent of Ṣāliḥ's people.

zajjaj:49-49.t:
﴿قالُوا تَقاسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ وأهْلَهُ ثُمَّ لَنَقُولَنَّ لِوَلِيِّهِ﴾: "لَتُبَيِّتُنَّهُ" is also permissible, and "لَيُبَيِّتُنَّهُ وأهْلَهُ" with yāʾ is permissible; there are three ways in it. Whoever reads with nūn reads: "ثُمَّ لَنَقُولَنَّ لِوَلِيِّهِ"; whoever reads "لَتُبَيِّتُنَّهُ" with tāʾ reads: "ثُمَّ لَتَقُولُنَّ"; and whoever reads "لَيُبَيِّتُنَّهُ" with yāʾ reads: "ثُمَّ لَيَقُولُنَّ لِوَلِيِّهِ".
Whoever reads with nūn, it is as if they said: "Swear: we will surely attack him and his family by night (اِحْلِفُوا لَنُبَيِّتَنَّهُ وأهْلَهُ)". Whoever reads with tāʾ, it is as if they said: "Swear: you will surely attack him by night (اِحْلِفُوا لَتُبَيِّتُنَهُ)", so it is as if the speaker excluded himself in wording. The nūn is better in reading. It is also possible that he included himself in the tāʾ, because when he says "تَقاسَمُوا" he has said "swear to one another (تَحالَفُوا)", and he does not exclude himself from the mutual oath. Whoever reads: "قالُوا تَقاسَمُوا بِاللَّهِ لِيُبَيِّتُنَّهُ", then the meaning is: "they said, 'they will surely attack him by night', swearing to one another (قالُوا لِيُبَيِّتُنَّهُ مُتَقاسِمِينَ)". [Translator's note: the source vocalises this as لِيُبَيِّتُنَّهُ, with kasra.] So this band had sworn to one another to attack Ṣāliḥ by night and kill him and his family in their night raid, then to deny before Ṣāliḥ's kinsmen that they had witnessed his destruction and the destruction of his family, and to swear that they were truthful. This was a plot they had resolved upon.

zajjaj:50-50.t: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿وَمَكَرُوا مَكْرًا ومَكَرْنا مَكْرًا وهم لا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾. So they went off to carry out their aim, and Allah sent a rock upon them which crushed their heads, and He sent upon the rest of their people that by which He killed them.

zajjaj:51-51.t: And His saying: ﴿فانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ أنّا دَمَّرْناهم وقَوْمَهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾: it is read "إنّا دَمَّرْناهم" with kasra of "إنَّ", and with fatḥa. Whoever reads with kasra puts al-ʿāqiba in the nominative and nothing else; the meaning is: "So look what thing was the outcome of their plotting (فانْظُرْ أيَّ شَيْءٍ كانَ عاقِبَةَ مَكْرِهِمْ)", then He explained it, saying: "إنّا دَمَّرْناهم", which shows that the outcome was destruction. [Translator's note: the source's paraphrase vocalises عاقِبَةَ in the accusative although it has just said the word is nominative.] Whoever reads "أنّا دَمَّرْناهم" with fatḥa puts al-ʿāqiba in the nominative, and if he wishes in the accusative; the nominative is better, with the meaning: "So look how was the outcome of their affair (فانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةَ أمْرِهِمْ)", and al-ʿāqiba is implied [again before] "أنّا دَمَّرْناهم", so "أنّا" is in the position of a nominative (fī mawḍiʿ rafʿ) on this interpretation. It may also be that "أنّا" is in the position of an accusative, with the meaning: "So look how was the outcome of their plotting, because we destroyed them (فانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهِمْ لِأنّا دَمَّرْناهم)". It may also be that "أنّا دَمَّرْناهم" is the khabar (predicate) of "كانَ"; the meaning: "So look how the outcome of their plotting was the destruction (فانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ عاقِبَةُ مَكْرِهُمُ الدَّمارَ)". It may also be that the noun (ism) of "كانَ" is "أنّا دَمَّرْناهم", and "عاقِبَةُ أمْرِهِمْ" is in the accusative; the meaning: "So look how the destruction was the outcome of their plotting (فانْظُرْ كَيْفَ كانَ الدَّمارُ عاقِبَةَ مَكْرِهِمْ)". "كَيْفَ" is in the position of an accusative in all of these views. Its accusative, when al-ʿāqiba is made the ism of "كانَ" and "كَيْفَ" the khabar, is because it is in the position of the khabar of "كانَ". When [al-ʿāqiba] is made the ism of "كانَ" and its khabar is what comes after it, then [كَيْفَ] is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), and the sentence as a whole governs it, just as you say: "How was Zayd? (كَيْفَ كانَ زَيْدٌ؟)" and "How was Zayd standing? (كَيْفَ كانَ زَيْدٌ قائِمًا؟)".

zajjaj:52-52.t: And His saying: ﴿فَتِلْكَ بُيُوتُهم خاوِيَةً بِما ظَلَمُوا﴾: most of the readers put "خاوِيَةً" in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning: "So look at their houses, empty, because of the wrong they did (فانْظُرْ إلى بُيُوتِهِمْ خاوِيَةً بِما ظَلَمُوا)". Its nominative is from four aspects, which we have already explained regarding whoever read: "وَهَذا بَعْلِي شَيْخٌ".

zajjaj:54-54.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَلُوطًا إذْ قالَ لِقَوْمِهِ﴾: the accusative of "لُوطًا" is from two angles: with the meaning "And We sent Lot (وَأرْسَلْنا لُوطًا)", and with the meaning "And remember Lot (واذْكُرْ لُوطًا)", when he said to his people; because stories of messengers have been running on, so the sense of an implied "remember (اُذْكُرْ)" enters here. ﴿أتَأْتُونَ الفاحِشَةَ وأنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ﴾, i.e. while you know that it is an indecency, so it is greater for your sins.

zajjaj:55-55.t: ﴿أإنَّكم لَتَأْتُونَ الرِّجالَ﴾: it is permissible in several ways: "آئِنَّكم", with two hamzas with an alif between them; "أئِنَّكم", with two fully pronounced hamzas is also permissible; and the best is "أيِنَّكم", making the second hamza bayna bayna (in between), so that it is between the yāʾ and the hamza.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
﴿فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إلا أنْ قالُوا﴾: "جَوابَ" is the khabar (predicate) of "كانَ", and "أنْ قالُوا" is the ism (noun). "فَما كانَ جَوابُ قَوْمِهِ إلّا أنْ قالُوا" is also permissible.
And His saying: ﴿إنَّهم أُناسٌ يَتَطَهَّرُونَ﴾: Lot's people said this to Lot and to those who believed with him, by way of mocking them, because they kept themselves pure from the backsides of men and the backsides of women. It is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar that he was asked: "Is this permissible with women?" — it was said to him: "What do you say about al-taḥmīḍ?" — and he said: "Do Muslims do that?" So this is very grave indeed, and it is what Allah named "an indecency (فاحِشَةً)".

zajjaj:59-59.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿آللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾, and "تُشْرِكُونَ", with yāʾ and with tāʾ. It is also read "آللَّهُ" and "اَللَّهُ", with madd and without madd. And it is permissible — and Allah knows best —: "اِللَّهُ خَيْرٌ أمْ ما يُشْرِكُونَ". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: When the tāʾ and the yāʾ take ḍamma, its meaning is that they made partners for Allah; and when the tāʾ and the rāʾ take fatḥa, its meaning is that you make yourselves partners to Allah. One says: "شَرِكْتُ الرَّجُلَ، أشْرَكُهُ" when I became his partner. [Translator's note: so in the source ("the tāʾ and the rāʾ"), i.e. the form تَشْرَكُونَ.]

zajjaj:60-60.t:
And His saying: ﴿حَدائِقَ ذاتَ بَهْجَةٍ﴾: "al-ḥadāʾiq (الحَدائِقُ)", its singular is "ḥadīqa (حَدِيقَةٌ)", and "al-ḥadīqa" is the garden (al-bustān), and likewise the walled garden (al-ḥāʾiṭ); and it was said: a plot of date palms. And His saying "ذاتَ بَهْجَةٍ" means: possessing beauty. Outside the reading, "ذَواتَ بَهْجَةٍ" is permissible, because they are a group, just as you say: "your women are possessed of beauty (نِسْوَتُكَ ذَواتُ حُسْنٍ)". "ذاتَ بَهْجَةٍ" is permissible only because a feminine plural may be spoken of with the singular feminine form when you mean a group, as if you said: "a group possessing beauty (جَماعَةً ذاتَ بَهْجَةٍ)".
And His saying: ﴿بَلْ هم قَوْمٌ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾ means: "they disbelieve (يَكْفُرُونَ)", i.e. they turn aside from the right course and the way of truth.

zajjaj:61-61.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَ البَحْرَيْنِ حاجِزًا﴾: He separated them by His power, so the fresh does not mix with the salt.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ لا يَعْلَمُ مَن في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ الغَيْبَ إلا اللَّهُ﴾: the reading is with the nominative; the accusative is permissible, but I know of no one who read it, so do not read it. Whoever puts ﴿إلا اللَّهُ﴾ in the nominative does so as a badal (substitute); the meaning: "No one knows the unseen except Allah (لا يَعْلَمُ أحَدٌ الغَيْبَ إلّا اللَّهُ)", i.e. none knows the unseen except Allah. Whoever puts it in the accusative does so with the meaning: "No one knows the unseen except Allah", in the sense of: "I except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for He knows the unseen (أسْتَثْنِي اللَّهَ - عَزَّ وجَلَّ - فَإنَّهُ يَعْلَمُ الغَيْبَ)".
And His saying: ﴿وَما يَشْعُرُونَ أيّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾, and "أيّانَ تُبْعَثُونَ" — both; i.e. "they do not know when the resurrection is".

zajjaj:66-66.t: And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿بَلِ ادّارَكَ عِلْمُهم في الآخِرَةِ﴾: there are several ways in it. Abū ʿAmr read: "بَلْ أُدْرِكَ عِلْمُهم في الآخِرَةِ"; most people read "بَلِ ادّارَكَ" with a doubled dāl; it was narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: "بَلى أدْرَكَ عِلْمُهم في الآخِرَةِ"; and "بَلى ادّارَكَ عِلْمُهم في الآخِرَةِ" is permissible. [Translator's note: the source vocalises Abū ʿAmr's reading as أُدْرِكَ; it is usually given as أَدْرَكَ.] Whoever reads "بَلِ ادّارَكَ عِلْمُهم في الآخِرَةِ" — and it is the good one — does so with the meaning "بَلْ تَدارَكَ عِلْمُهم في الآخِرَةِ", in the sense of "rather their knowledge will become complete on the Day of Resurrection", because they will be resurrected and everything they were promised is true. Whoever reads "بَلْ أدْرَكَ عِلْمُهم" does so with the sense of affirmation-seeking and inquiry (al-taqrīr wa-l-istikhbār), as if it were said: "Their knowledge has not attained [anything] concerning the Hereafter (لَمْ يُدْرِكْ عِلْمُهم في الآخِرَةِ)", i.e. "they do not, in this world, come to know its reality"; then He made that clear in His saying: ﴿بَلْ هم في شَكٍّ مِنها﴾. They said in explaining "بَلِ ادّارَكَ عِلْمُهم": "أمْ أدْرَكَ عِلْمُهم". The good reading is "اِدّارَكَ", in the sense of "تَدارَكَ", with the tāʾ assimilated into the dāl, so it becomes a dāl with sukūn; one cannot begin with it, so one brings the connective alif (alif al-waṣl) in order to be able to pronounce it. When you pause on "بَلْ" and begin anew, you say "اِدّارَكَ"; when you join, you give the lām of "بَلْ" a kasra because of its sukūn and the sukūn of the dāl.

zajjaj:70-70.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَكُنْ في ضَيْقٍ مِمّا يَمْكُرُونَ﴾: it is read "في ضَيْقٍ" and "ضِيقٍ".

zajjaj:72-72.t: And His saying: ﴿عَسى أنْ يَكُونَ رَدِفَ لَكم بَعْضُ الَّذِي تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾: it was said in the exegesis: "hastened for you". Its meaning in the language is: "رَدِفَكم" is like "it rode behind you (رَكِبَكم)" and "it came after you (جاءَ بَعْدَكم)".

zajjaj:81-81.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَما أنْتَ بِهادِي العُمْيِ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ﴾: it is also read "وَما أنْتَ تَهْدِي العُمْيَ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ", and "بِهادٍ العُمْيَ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ" is permissible. As for the first two ways, they are good in reading and both have been read; the third way is permissible in Arabic, but unless a transmission of it is established it is not to be read, and I know of no one who read it.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنْ تُسْمِعُ إلا مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِآياتِنا﴾ means: you do not make anyone hear except one who believes. The interpretation of "ما تُسْمِعُ" is: no one hears from you, takes it in and acts on it, except one who believes in Our signs. As for one who hears and does not accept, he is in the position of the deaf, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 18]. The poet said:
؎أصَمُّ عَمّا ساءَهُ سَمِيعُ
(Deaf to what displeases him, [yet] hearing.)

zajjaj:82-82.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإذا وقَعَ القَوْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, i.e. when it becomes due. ﴿أخْرَجْنا لَهم دابَّةً مِنَ الأرْضِ تُكَلِّمُهُمْ﴾, and "تَكْلِمُهم". It is narrated that the first of the signs of the Hour is the emergence of the beast and the rising of the sun from its place of setting. Most of what has come in the exegesis is that it will emerge in Tihāma, emerging from between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa. It has also come in the exegesis that it will emerge three times, in three places. And it has come in the exegesis: "It will make a black spot on the face of the disbeliever and a white spot on the face of the believer; the disbeliever's spot will spread until his whole face is blackened by it, and the believer's spot will spread until his face is whitened by it; then the group will gather at the table, and the believer will be known from the disbeliever." Whoever reads "تُكَلِّمُهم" takes it from "al-kalām (الكَلامُ)", speech; and whoever reads "تَكْلِمُهم" takes it from "al-kalm (الكَلْمُ)", which is the mark and the wound.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
And His saying: ﴿صُنْعَ اللَّهِ الَّذِي أتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾: the reading is the accusative, and the nominative "صُنْعُ" is permissible. Whoever puts it in the accusative does so in the sense of the maṣdar (verbal noun), because His saying ﴿وَتَرى الجِبالَ تَحْسَبُها جامِدَةً وهي تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحابِ﴾ indicates the making, as if it were said: "Allah made that, a making (صَنَعَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ صُنْعًا)". Whoever says "صُنْعُ اللَّهِ" in the nominative, the meaning is: "That is the making of Allah (ذَلِكَ صُنْعُ اللَّهِ)".
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَكُلٌّ أتَوْهُ داخِرِينَ﴾ [al-Naml: 87], and "أتاهُ داخِرِينَ": whoever uses the singular does so for the wording of "كُلٌّ", and whoever uses the plural does so for its meaning.

zajjaj:91-91.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّما أُمِرْتُ أنْ أعْبُدَ رَبَّ هَذِهِ البَلْدَةِ الَّذِي حَرَّمَها﴾: "الَّذِي" is in the position of an accusative, as an attribute of "رَبَّ هَذِهِ البَلْدَةِ". It has been read "الَّتِي حَرَّمَها" — it has been read so, but it is rare — and then "الَّتِي" is in the position of a genitive (khafḍ), as a naʿt (adjective) of "البَلْدَةِ".

zajjaj:93-93.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سَيُرِيكم آياتِهِ فَتَعْرِفُونَها﴾, i.e. Allah will show you His signs in all that He has created, and in yourselves.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Naml
Meccan
﷽
﴿طس﴾ — Ibn ʿAbbās said: "طس" is one of the names of Allah the Exalted, by which He swore. Qatāda said: "It is one of the names of the Quran".
His saying: ﴿تِلْكَ آياتُ القُرْآنِ وكِتابٍ مُبِينٍ﴾: the meaning of "تِلْكَ" is that they had been promised the Quran in their scriptures, so it was said to them: "these are those verses which you were promised". We have explained what is in this at the beginning of Sūrat "al-Baqara". "كِتابٍ" is genitive (makhfūḍ) on the meaning: "these are the verses of the Quran, the verses of a clear Book". "وكِتابٌ مُبِينٌ" is also permissible, but I know of no one who read it so; the meaning would then be: "these are the verses of the Quran, and that is a clear Book".

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿هُدًى وبُشْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: it is possible that "هُدًى" is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "these are the verses of the Book, guiding and giving good tidings". It is also possible that it is in the position of the nominative for one of two reasons. One of them is on the implying of "it is guidance and good tidings"; and if you wish, as a badal (substitute) for "آياتُ", on the meaning: "these are guidance and good tidings"; and if you wish, as a badal for "آياتُ", on the meaning: "these are guidance and good tidings" [Translator's note: this clause is repeated in the source]. In the nominative there is a good third way: that it be a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, both of them together being the khabar of "تِلْكَ", on the meaning of their saying "هو حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ" (it is sweet-sour), that is: it combines both tastes. So the khabar of "تِلْكَ" is "آياتُ" and its (further) khabar is "هُدًى وبُشْرى", so you combine (the statements) that they are "verses" and that they are "guiding and giving good tidings".

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالآخِرَةِ زَيَّنّا لَهم أعْمالَهُمْ﴾, that is: We made their requital for their disbelief that We made what they are engaged in seem fair to them. ﴿فَهم يَعْمَهُونَ﴾, that is: they wander in confusion. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
أعْمى الهُدى بِالجاهِلِينَ العُمَّهِ
(Blind to guidance among the ignorant who wander in confusion.)

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَإنَّكَ لَتُلَقّى القُرْآنَ مِن لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾, that is: the Quran is cast to you as revelation from Allah; He sent it down with His knowledge and His wisdom.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إذْ قالَ مُوسى لأهْلِهِ إنِّي آنَسْتُ نارًا﴾: the position of "إذْ" is accusative; the meaning is: "remember when Moses said to his family", that is: remember the story of Moses. The meaning of ﴿آنَسْتُ نارًا﴾ is: I have seen a fire.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أوْ آتِيكم بِشِهابٍ قَبَسٍ﴾ — it is read with tanwīn and with iḍāfa (annexation). Whoever reads it with tanwīn makes "قَبَسٍ" a naʿt (adjective) of "شِهابٍ"; and everything white possessing light is a shihāb.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لَعَلَّكم تَصْطَلُونَ﴾ — it came in the exegesis that they were in winter, and for that reason they needed to warm themselves.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَها﴾, that is: when Moses came to the fire, ﴿نُودِيَ أنْ بُورِكَ مَن في النّارِ ومَن حَوْلَها﴾. The position of "أنْ": if you wish it is accusative, and if you wish it is nominative. Whoever judges it accusative, the meaning is: "Moses was called with (the words) that whoever is in the fire has been blessed", and the noun whose agent is not named (the nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent) is implied in "نُودِيَ". Whoever judges it nominative, it is the noun whose agent is not named, that is: "it was called out that … has been blessed". It came in the exegesis that "مَن في النّارِ" here is the light of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and "مَن حَوْلَها": it was said: the angels; and it was said: "the light of Allah".
His saying: ﴿وَسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ means: declaring Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, free of all evil. So it came from the Prophet ﷺ, and so the lexicographers explained it.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا رَآها تَهْتَزُّ كَأنَّها جانٌّ﴾, that is: moving, as the jānn moves with a light motion, while it was in the form of the thuʿbān, which is the large kind of snake. ﴿وَلّى مُدْبِرًا ولَمْ يُعَقِّبْ﴾ — it came in the exegesis that "لَمْ يُعَقِّبْ" means: he did not look back; and it also came: he did not return. The lexicographers say: he did not return; one says "قَدْ عَقَّبَ فُلانٌ" when he returns to fight after having turned away. Labīd said:
حَتّى تَهَجَّرَ في الرَّواحِ وهاجَهُ ∗∗∗ طَلَبُ المُعَقِّبِ حَقَّهُ المَظْلُومُ
(Until he set out in the midday heat for the evening journey, roused like the wronged one who returns again to seek his right.)
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنِّي لا يَخافُ لَدَيَّ المُرْسَلُونَ﴾ means: "the messengers do not fear in My presence".

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿إلا مَن ظَلَمَ﴾: "إلّا" is an exception not from (the kind of) the first; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "but whoever does wrong and then repents, among the messengers and others"; and that is His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَّلَ حُسْنًا بَعْدَ سُوءٍ فَإنِّي غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَأدْخِلْ يَدَكَ في جَيْبِكَ تَخْرُجْ بَيْضاءَ مِن غَيْرِ سُوءٍ﴾: the meaning is: "put your hand into the opening of your garment and bring it out; it will come out white without harm". It came in the exegesis: "مِن غَيْرِ سُوءٍ" means without leprosy. It also came that he was wearing a woollen tunic without sleeves.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فِي تِسْعِ آياتٍ إلى فِرْعَوْنَ وقَوْمِهِ﴾: "في" is connected to His saying "and throw down your staff, and put your hand"; so the interpretation is: "and display these two signs among nine signs", and its interpretation is: "from among signs". It came in the exegesis that the nine are: "his hand being white without harm, the staff being a snake, the drought that afflicted the people of Pharaoh in their open country, the deficiency of fruits from their farmlands, the sending of locusts upon them, and lice, and frogs, and blood, and the flood" — these are nine signs. Like His saying ﴿فِي تِسْعِ آياتٍ﴾, whose meaning is "out of nine", is their saying: "خُذْ لِي عَشْرًا مِنَ الإبِلِ فِيها فَحْلانِ" (take ten camels for me, among them two stallions); the meaning is: "of them two stallions".

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَتْهم آياتُنا مُبْصِرَةً﴾, that is: clear. "مُبْصَرَةً" is also permissible, and its meaning is: "made clear, seen and beheld".

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿واسْتَيْقَنَتْها أنْفُسُهم ظُلْمًا وعُلُوًّا﴾: the meaning is: "and they rejected them out of wrongdoing and arrogance (ʿuluww)", that is: disdaining to believe in what Moses, peace be upon him, brought. So they rejected them while knowing that they were from Allah.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَوَرِثَ سُلَيْمانُ داوُدَ﴾ — it came in the exegesis that he inherited from him his prophethood and his kingship. It is related that David had nineteen sons, and Solomon from among them inherited from him prophethood and kingship.
His saying: ﴿وَقالَ يا أيُّها النّاسُ عُلِّمْنا مَنطِقَ الطَّيْرِ﴾ — it came in the exegesis that it is the simple-minded (al-bulh) among them [Translator's note: as written]. I reckon — and Allah knows best — that it is what Allah inspired the birds with of that by which they glorify Him, as He said: ﴿وَسَخَّرْنا مَعَ داوُدَ الجِبالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ والطَّيْرَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 79].
His saying: ﴿وَأُوتِينا مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾: the meaning is: "we have been given of everything that it is possible for prophets and people to be given". Likewise His saying: ﴿وَأُوتِيَتْ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-Naml: 23], that is: of everything the like of her is given. People's speech runs on this basis; a speaker says: "everyone has come to so-and-so with his need", the meaning being: "many people have come to him".

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَحُشِرَ لِسُلَيْمانَ جُنُودُهُ مِنَ الجِنِّ والإنْسِ والطَّيْرِ فَهم يُوزَعُونَ﴾: in the language "يُوزَعُونَ" means: they are held back. It came in the exegesis: "the first of them are held back, and the first of them are detained for the last of them".

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿حَتّى إذا أتَوْا عَلى وادِ النَّمْلِ﴾ — it is related that this Valley of the Ants was in Syria, and that the ants of Solomon, peace be upon him, were the size of flies. ﴿قالَتْ نَمْلَةٌ يا أيُّها النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَساكِنَكُمْ﴾ — the wording "اُدْخُلُوا" came like the wording used for rational beings: one says to people "اُدْخُلُوا", and likewise to angels and jinn, and likewise "دَخَلُوا". When you mention ants you say "قَدْ دَخَلْنَ" and "دَخَلَتْ", and likewise all non-rational things; except that the ants here were treated like human beings when they spoke as human beings speak. ﴿لا يَحْطِمَنَّكم سُلَيْمانُ وجُنُودُهُ﴾ — it is also read "لا تَحْطِمَنَّكم سُلَيْمانُ" and "لا تُحَطِّمَنَّكم سُلَيْمانُ"; and "لا يُحَطِّمَنَّكم" is permissible.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿فَتَبَسَّمَ ضاحِكًا مِن قَوْلِها﴾ — because most of the laughter of the prophets, peace be upon them, is smiling. "ضاحِكًا" is accusative, an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because "تَبَسَّمَ" has the meaning of "ضَحِكَ". ﴿وَقالَ رَبِّ أوْزِعْنِي أنْ أشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ﴾: the meaning of "أوْزِعْنِي" is: inspire me; and its interpretation in the language is: restrain me from (other) things except from thanking for Your favour, that is: "restrain me from what would distance (me) from You". ﴿وَأنْ أعْمَلَ صالِحًا تَرْضاهُ﴾.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَتَفَقَّدَ الطَّيْرَ فَقالَ ما لِيَ لا أرى الهُدْهُدَ أمْ كانَ مِنَ الغائِبِينَ﴾ — with fatḥa on the yāʾ and with it quiescent in "ما لِيَ"; the fatḥa is better, and we have explained that. His saying "أمْ كانَ مِنَ الغائِبِينَ" means: "rather, was he among the absent?". It came in the exegesis that Solomon ﷺ looked for the hoopoe because it was the water-surveyor: when Solomon, peace be upon him, halted in a desert of the earth, he learned from the hoopoe the distance to the water. It was said that the hoopoe sees water in the earth as water is seen in a glass vessel.

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لأُعَذِّبَنَّهُ عَذابًا شَدِيدًا أوْ لأذْبَحَنَّهُ﴾ — it is related that Solomon's punishment of birds was to pluck the feathers of the bird's wing and have it thrown into the sun. ﴿أوْ لَيَأْتِيَنِّي بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, that is: or he will bring me an argument for his absence.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَكَثَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ﴾ — it is also read "فَمَكُثَ", with ḍamma on the kāf, and with fatḥa; that is: not a long time.
His saying: ﴿فَقالَ أحَطْتُ بِما لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ﴾: the meaning is: "then the hoopoe came, and Solomon asked him about his absence, and he said: I have encompassed what you have not encompassed"; this was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech. The meaning of "أحَطْتُ" is: I have known a thing from all its sides; you say "أحَطْتُ بِهَذا عِلْمًا", that is: I knew all of it; nothing of it remained hidden from me.
His saying: ﴿وَجِئْتُكَ مِن سَبَإٍ بِنَبَإٍ يَقِينٍ﴾ — it is read as a triptote (with ṣarf) and tanwīn, and it is read "مِن سَبَأ" with fatḥa on "سَبَأ" and without tanwīn. As for whoever does not treat it as a triptote, he makes it the name of a city. As for whoever does treat it as a triptote: some of the grammarians mentioned that it is the name of a single man, and others mentioned that when a name is not known for what it is, it is not inflected as a triptote. One of these two statements is a mistake, because nouns are entitled to full inflection (ṣarf); so when it is not known whether a noun is for a masculine or a feminine, it is entitled to full inflection until it is known that it is a diptote, because the basic state of nouns is full inflection, and every diptote is given full inflection in poetry. As for those who said that "سَبَأٌ" is the name of a man, that too is an error, because "سَبَأٌ" is a city known as "مَأْرِبٌ", in Yemen, three days' journey from Ṣanʿāʾ. The poet said:
مِن سَبَأ الحاضِرِينَ مَأْرِبَ إذْ ∗∗∗ يَبْنُونَ مِن دُونِ سَيْلِها العَرِما
(Of Sabaʾ, those dwelling at Maʾrib, when they built the dam against its torrent.)
So whoever does not treat it as a triptote does so because it is the name of a city; and whoever treats it as a triptote — and full inflection is more common in recitation — does so because it is a name for the land (al-balad), and so is a masculine named with a masculine. If a report is sound about it (being a man's name), it is only that the city was named after a man.

zajjaj:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَأُوتِيَتْ مِن كُلِّ شَيْءٍ ولَها عَرْشٌ﴾ means: "and she has been given of everything that kings are given and people are given". "اَلْعَرْشُ" is a great throne.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿ألا يَسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ الَّذِي يُخْرِجُ الخَبْءَ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ — it is also read "ألا يَسْجُدُوا" [Translator's note: so in the source; the two readings meant are «ألّا يَسْجُدُوا» with doubling and «ألا يا اسْجُدُوا» without it, as the following discussion shows]. Whoever read it with the doubling, the meaning is: "and Satan made their deeds seem fair to them and so turned them away (from the path), so that they do not prostrate", that is: "so he turned them away so that they would not prostrate to Allah". The position of "أنْ" is accusative by His saying "فَصَدَّهم", and its position may be genitive even though the lām has been omitted. Whoever read it without the doubling, then "ألا" is for opening speech and for drawing attention (tanbīh), and the pause on it is "ألا يا"; then he begins anew and says: "اُسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ" (prostrate to Allah). For whoever reads it without the doubling, it is a place of prostration in the Quran; and whoever reads "ألّا يَسْجُدُوا" with the doubling, it is not a place of prostration. Like His saying "ألا يا اسْجُدُوا" without the doubling is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma:
ألا يا اسْلَمِي يا دارَ مَيَّ عَلى البِلى ∗∗∗ ولا زالَ مُنْهَلًّا بِجَرْعائِكِ القَطْرُ
(Ho! Be safe, O abode of Mayya, despite decay, and may the rain never cease to pour on your sandy ground.)
And al-Akhṭal said:
ألا يا اسْلَمِي يا هِنْدُ هِنْدَ بَنِي بَدْرِ ∗∗∗ تَحِيَّةَ مَن صَلّى فُؤادَكِ بِالجَمْرِ
(Ho! Be safe, O Hind, Hind of the Banū Badr — the greeting of one who has scorched your heart with live coals.)
And al-ʿAjjāj said:
يا دارَ سَلْمى يا اسْلَمِي ثُمَّ اسْلَمِي ∗∗∗ بِسَمْسَمٍ أوْ عَنْ يَمِينِ سَمْسَمِ
(O abode of Salmā, ho! be safe, and again be safe, at Samsam or to the right of Samsam.)
We have multiplied the evidence for this word only as those before us did; and they did that only because the common people are little accustomed to the entry of "يا" other than in the vocative: the common people hardly say "يا قَدْ قَدِمَ زَيْدٌ" or "يا اذْهَبْ بِسَلامٍ".
His saying: ﴿لِلَّهِ الَّذِي يُخْرِجُ الخَبْءَ في السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾: everything you have hidden is khabʾ. It came in the exegesis that the khabʾ here is the rain from the sky and the vegetation from the earth. It is also possible — and it is the (right) way — that the khabʾ is everything hidden, so the meaning is: "He knows the unseen in the heavens and the earth"; the proof of this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ ما تُخْفُونَ وما تُعْلِنُونَ﴾.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
In His saying, the Exalted: ﴿فَألْقِهْ إلَيْهِمْ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ﴾ there are five ways: "فَألْقِهِي إلَيْهِمْ", keeping the yāʾ, and it is the most common reading; "فَألْقِهِ إلَيْهِمْ" is permissible, omitting the yāʾ and keeping the kasra, because its origin is "فَألْقِيهِ إلَيْهِمْ", and the yāʾ was omitted for the jussive (jazm) — I mean the yāʾ of "ألْقِيهِ"; "فَألْقِهُو إلَيْهِمْ" is permissible, keeping the wāw; "فَألْقِهُ إلَيْهِمْ" is permissible, with ḍamma and the wāw omitted; and "فَألْقِهْ إلَيْهِمْ" has been read, with the hāʾ quiescent. As for keeping the yāʾ, "فَألْقِهِي", it is the best of them, for the yāʾ that drops for the jussive has already dropped before the hāʾ, because the origin is "فَألْقِيهِ إلَيْهِمْ". Whoever omitted the yāʾ and left the kasra after the hāʾ did so because, when the yāʾ is kept, as in your saying "أنا أُلْقِيهِ إلَيْهِمْ", the preferred choice is to omit the yāʾ that comes after the hāʾ; we have explained that sufficiently at His saying ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ إلَيْكَ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 75]. Whoever read "فَألْقِهُو إلَيْهِمْ" returned it to its origin, the origin being to keep the wāw with the pronominal hāʾ: you say "ألْقَيْتُهُو إلَيْكَ". By our saying "keeping the wāw and the yāʾ" I mean in pronunciation and in continuous speech; when you pause, you pause on a hāʾ, and when you write, you write with a hāʾ. Whoever read it omitting the wāw and keeping the ḍamma, that is like omitting the yāʾ and keeping the kasra. Whoever made the hāʾ quiescent is in error, because the hāʾ is not jussive; yet it has a basis in analogy, which is that the hāʾ is treated in continuous speech as it is in the pause. Most often this occurs in poetry, where this (vowel) is dropped from the hāʾ and a kasra remains [Translator's note: as written; the verse cited shows the hāʾ made quiescent]. The poet said:
فَإنْ يَكُ غَثًّا أوْ سَمِينًا فَإنَّنِي ∗∗∗ سَأجْعَلُ عَيْنَيْهِ لِنَفْسِهْ مَقْنَعا
(Whether it be lean or fat, I will make his eyes the judge of what satisfies him.)
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهم فانْظُرْ ماذا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ — there are two statements about it. Some said: its meaning involves placing earlier and later (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr); its meaning is: "go with this letter of mine and cast it to them, and see what they return; then turn away from them". He said this because his returning from them and turning away from them comes after he sees what the answer is. This is good, and placing earlier and later is common in speech. And they (others) said: the meaning of "ثُمَّ تَوَلَّ عَنْهم" is: "turn away from them, concealing yourself where they do not see you, and see what answer they give back".

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قالَتْ يا أيُّها المَلأُ إنِّي أُلْقِيَ إلَيَّ كِتابٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ — so the hoopoe went and cast the letter to them, and heard her saying: "O assembly…"; this was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech. The meaning of ﴿كِتابٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ is: its contents are good.

zajjaj:30-30.t: Then she made clear what was in it, saying: ﴿إنَّهُ مِن سُلَيْمانَ وإنَّهُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ ﴿ألا تَعْلُوا عَلَيَّ وأْتُونِي مُسْلِمِينَ﴾ [al-Naml: 31]. This is what was in the letter; the letters of the prophets — the blessings of Allah be upon them — follow brevity and concision. It has been related that the letter was: "From the servant of Allah, Solomon, to Bilqīs daughter of Sharāḥīl" [Translator's note: the source spells the name سَراحِيل]; and people only write "from the servant of Allah" in imitation of Solomon. The meaning of ﴿ألا تَعْلُوا عَلَيَّ﴾ [al-Naml: 31] is: "do not exalt yourselves above me, even if you are kings".

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها المَلأُ أفْتُونِي في أمْرِي﴾, that is: make clear to me what I should do. "اَلْمَلَأُ" are the notables of the people, who are capable (milāʾ) of what is needed.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
﴿قالُوا نَحْنُ أُولُو قُوَّةٍ وأُولُو بَأْسٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾ — it is related that she had with her a thousand qayl, "اَلْقَيْلُ" being a king (chieftain), and with every qayl a thousand men; and it was said: a hundred thousand men, and most reports say a hundred thousand men.
His saying: ﴿حَتّى تَشْهَدُونِ﴾ [al-Naml: 32] — with kasra on the nūn; fatḥa on the nūn is not permissible, because its origin is "حَتّى تَشْهَدُونَنِي": the first nūn was omitted for the accusative (naṣb), and the nūn and yāʾ of the (pronoun) noun remained; then the yāʾ was omitted because the kasra indicates it, and because it is the end of a verse. Whoever gives the nūn fatḥa commits a solecism (laḥn), because when the nūn has fatḥa it is the nūn of the indicative (rafʿ), and this is not one of the cases in which "حَتّى" is followed by the indicative. It is permissible to say "أنَّهُ مِن سُلَيْمانَ وأنَّهُ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ" with fatḥa on the alif; the position of "أنَّ" would then be nominative, on the meaning: "it was cast to me that it is from Solomon". It is also possible for "أنَّ" to be in the position of the accusative, on the meaning: "a noble letter, because it is from Solomon and because it is in the name of Allah, the All-Merciful, the Most Merciful". As for "ألّا تَعْلُوا عَلَيَّ", "أنْ" may be in the position of the nominative or the accusative. The accusative is on the meaning: "a letter (enjoining) that you not exalt yourselves above me", that is: "it was written with the abandoning of haughtiness"; and it is permissible on the meaning: "it was cast to me that you should not exalt yourselves above me". There is another good way in it, on the meaning: "he said: do not exalt yourselves above me". Sībawayh and al-Khalīl explained that "أنْ" in this place has the sense of "أيْ" (namely), on the meaning: "namely: do not exalt yourselves above me". Like it in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is: ﴿وانْطَلَقَ المَلأُ مِنهم أنِ امْشُوا﴾ [Ṣād: 6]. The sense of "أيْ" here is the sense of speech and explanation, as you say: "so-and-so did such-and-such, i.e.: I am generous", as though you said: "he says: I am generous".

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿قالَتْ إنَّ المُلُوكَ إذا دَخَلُوا قَرْيَةً أفْسَدُوها وجَعَلُوا أعِزَّةَ أهْلِها أذِلَّةً﴾ means: when they enter it by force, through fighting and conquest. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ is from the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic — and Allah knows best — because she had already mentioned that they cause corruption, so there would be no benefit in her repeating this.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإنِّي مُرْسِلَةٌ إلَيْهِمْ بِهَدِيَّةٍ﴾ — it came in the exegesis that she presented Solomon with a brick of gold in silk; and it was said: bricks of gold in silk. Solomon ordered a gold brick, and it was thrown beneath the riding animals, where the animals would urinate and drop dung on it; so what they had brought to Solomon became small in their eyes. It has been mentioned that the gift was something other than this; but Solomon's saying ﴿أتُمِدُّونَنِ بِمالٍ﴾ [al-Naml: 36] is among what indicates that the gift was wealth.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿بِمَ يَرْجِعُ المُرْسَلُونَ﴾: with the prepositions together with "ما" in a question, the alif of "ما" is omitted, because the two are like a single thing, and in order to distinguish between a statement and a question. You say "قَدْ رَغِبْتُ فِيما عِنْدَكَ" (I have desired what you have), keeping the alif; and you say "فِيمَ نَظَرْتَ يا هَذا؟" (What did you look into, you there?), omitting the alif.
